title: Live OEE dashboard for a 3-machine CNC cell (example data)
summary: Availability x performance x quality, per machine, right now. Example data from a fictional cell - the board is the point, the numbers are the illustration.

blocks.title: One number per machine, three numbers behind it
blocks.body: OEE - overall equipment effectiveness - multiplies availability (was it running?), performance (was it running at rate?), and quality (was the output good?). A 3-machine cell, second shift, fictional data. The board answers 'how is the cell doing' in one glance and 'why' in one more.

blocks.heading: Per machine, right now
blocks.caption: All figures fictional but internally consistent. Mill 3's quality drag is a chatter problem wearing inserts early.

blocks.heading: How each number is earned
blocks.body: Availability is run time over planned time: Mill 2's 23-minute stop against a 100-minute window is 77 minutes over... no - availability counts all planned production time, and at 61% the board is saying the machine has been down or idle over a third of the shift. Performance is actual rate over ideal rate while running: Mill 3 runs nearly always (95%) but at two-thirds of its programmed feed, usually the operator derating for chatter. Quality is good parts over total parts: 91% cell-wide means nine of every hundred parts are scrap or rework. Multiply the three and 0.81 x 0.79 x 0.91 lands at 58.3% - a thoroughly normal, thoroughly improvable cell.

blocks.heading: Where the 42 points went
rows: Probe batteries - a $4 part holding a $40/hour spindle
Chatter derate; insert and stick-out review tomorrow
Same root cause as the derate - fix the chatter twice, count it once
Chip bins, door cycles, and the walk to the crib

items.title: Shift start, all three up
items.detail: Cell OEE running 71% through the first hour - the best hour of the day, as usual.

items.title: Mill 3 starts chattering
items.detail: Operator derates to 66% feed. Performance loss begins; scrap follows within the hour.

items.title: Mill 2 down
items.detail: Probe batteries die mid-cycle. Maintenance dispatched; crib is out of stock; someone drives to the hardware store.

items.title: Mill 2 back
items.detail: Twenty-three minutes lost to a consumable that costs less than the coffee.

blocks.heading: How to operate on this board
items: Read the cell number, then immediately read the three factors - a low OEE with high availability is a different animal than one with low availability.
Find the reddest machine row and ask why before asking who.
Check the losses table against the story: does the biggest loss have an owner and a date?
Act on one loss per shift. Boards that spawn five action items spawn none.

blocks.title: What this board cannot tell you
blocks.body: OEE says nothing about whether the cell is running the right parts, whether the schedule itself is sane, or whether the ideal rates are honest. An 85% OEE on work nobody ordered is worse than 55% on the hot job. The number starts the conversation; it is never the conversation's end.
